correctness.rationale: With Cdot=f(C,B), Bdot=g(C,B), zdot=H(C,B) independent of z, vertical translations commute with the flow. An equilibrium of (f,g) with H=0 lifts to a one-dimensional equilibrium set, excluding attractivity of an individual point by perturbing z(0). For a T-periodic (C,B) orbit, integrate z(t+T)-z(t)=integral_t^{t+T} H(C(s),B(s))ds=Delta independent of t. Thus full T-periodicity iff Delta=0, and otherwise drift nDelta. Existence is conditional on cell equilibria and flux balance; no full-state equilibrium is asserted when H not zero. This is a direct rigorous calculus proof and needs no numerical proxy.
residual_risks: Does not establish signs of Delta for particular simulated orbits; z coordinate may be physically restricted to an interval, so only local interior translations are allowed.

value.rationale: The asserted conclusions are routine structural properties of any passive scalar integrator xdot=F(x), zdot=H(x): translation in z, no isolated point attractor, period integral closure. Chaiya et al already explicitly restrict their stability theorem to the 2D active subsystem, so no consequential mathematical error is corrected. No parameter-dependent flux sign, model-specific periodicity existence, quantitative balance boundary or new invariant is obtained. An accessible, potentially helpful explanatory caveat is not by itself a motivated new mathematical gap at the shared value bar.
residual_risks: A model-specific computed flux-balance boundary or demonstrated wrong full-state theorem could support a different, substantively expanded claim, but is not present; no repair attempted.

limitations: Scientific rejection for originality and value (not for correctness or unavailable literature); published source already frames stability as 2D. No corrected package or substantive different claim produced.
